claims.value: Human Papillomavirus-Independent Head and Neck Mucosal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
claims.evidence: HPV status is carried by the disease term (review round 1: the custom hpv status column was unlicensed and not an ontology term). NCIT:C207803 'Human Papillomavirus-Independent Head and Neck Mucosal Squamous Cell Carcinoma' (def. 'arises from the mucosal sites of the head and neck and is not associated with human papillomavirus infection') for the study's HPV- group: UM-SCC-4, -6, -10A, -18, -19, -23, -17A, -17B (Supplementary Data sheet 2 header 'HPV-'). NCIT:C171023 'Human Papillomavirus-Related Head and Neck Mucosal Squamous Cell Carcinoma' (def. '... associated with human papillomavirus infection') for the HPV+ group: UD-SCC-2, UM-SCC-104, 93-VU147-T, UPCI:SCC-90, -152, -154 (sheet 2 header 'HPV+'), plus UM-SCC-47 from Cellosaurus ('Contains from 21 to 47 copies of the HPV16 genome'; Transformant HPV16) - UM-SCC-47 is NOT in the paper's analysis (absent from sheet 2; paper 'HPV-negative and 6 HPV-positive'). Both terms verified live in OLS4 (not obsolete); no MONDO/EFO/DOID equivalent exists; the resolved sample-metadata disease validator lists ncit (warning level). All lines are mucosal head and neck SCC (Cellosaurus: tongue, larynx, hypopharynx, floor-of-mouth SCC; 17B = cervical lymph node metastasis of the laryngeal SCC of the 17A donor). The site-specific SCC term is dropped; the site remains in organism part. CONFLICT kept per study: Cellosaurus CVCL_7733 lists UM-SCC-23 as 'Transformant: HPV31', the study groups it HPV-. Heavy reference: breast cancer MONDO:0007254 (paper: 'breast cancer cell lines').

limitations: techsdrf is not installed; instrument, acquisition mode, NCE and MS1 range were read from HTTP-range-read .raw headers only.

No search-engine parameter file is deposited: EpiProfile 2.0 (targeted XIC extraction) parameters, including precursor/fragment tolerances, are not deposited or stated -> tolerances 'not available'. comment[modification parameters] is reconstructed from the paper's chemistry, ref44's EpiProfile/MaxQuant variable-modification list for the same protocols and the Arg10 heavy label of the lab's super-SILAC method (ref44/ref19), not read from a deposited search file.

The heavy label (Arg10, UNIMOD:267) is taken from the lab's published histone super-SILAC method (ref19 'Arg-10' SILAC-DMEM; ref44 'Arg10 was selected as heavy label (multiplicity = 2) in ... EpiProfile 2'), which this paper cites; this paper itself does not name the heavy amino acid, and no MS1 heavy/light mass offset was measured.

The cell lines making up the heavy super-SILAC reference mixes are not named in this paper (refs [42]/[43], not open access). Ref19 (2016) used MDA-MB-231, MDA-MB-468, MDA-MB-453 and MDA-MB-361 for its breast cancer mix, but it is not stated that the mix used here is identical, so the components are not listed.

reconcile reports instrument_contradicted (protocol names only Q Exactive Plus; 28 rows say Q Exactive HF). Refuted: the 28 HF* raw headers read 'Q Exactive HF - Orbitrap MS' and PRIDE lists Q Exactive HF; the paper prose is incomplete.
The 22 FFPE runs of this deposit are not annotated (review round 1, coordinator decision): no source keys the FFPE raw files to HPV status or patient; see annotations/BLOCKED.md and the report.
UM-SCC-23: the study classifies it HPV-negative (Supplementary Data sheet 2) -> HPV-independent HNSCC; Cellosaurus lists it as an HPV31 transformant. The study's grouping is used.

UM-SCC-47 (HF190703_RN_HN_47) is deposited but was NOT part of the paper's analysis (absent from Supplementary Data sheet 2; its EpiProfile .ms2 is ~1 MB vs 13-70 MB for the others, suggesting a failed run); its HPV-related disease term comes from Cellosaurus, not the paper.

HPV status is encoded via NCIT HPV-related/independent head and neck mucosal SCC terms in characteristics[disease]; the Cellosaurus site-specific SCC diagnosis (tongue/laryngeal/hypopharyngeal/floor-of-mouth SCC) is therefore not in the disease column (site kept in organism part).
Organism part for UM-SCC-4/6/18/19, UM-SCC-104 and UD-SCC-2 is derived from the Cellosaurus disease term's site (no 'Derived from site' line).
Cell-line derivatisation is D3-acetylation (paper: 'deuterated acetic anhydride (cell lines)'); no PIC step is stated for it, so no Phenylisocyanate mod is declared for this part.
